ety.text: First attested as а́ккула f (ákkula) in 1747 and 1789, а́ккулъ m (ákkul) in 1788, акулъ m (akul) in 1755. Likely inherited from Middle Russian (or possibly a back-formation), attested only as a derivative акулий (akulij) used to describe liver oil of a Greenland shark in a source going back to late 16th or early 17th century. Borrowed from Sami language (compare Skolt Sami akkli, Kildin Sami а̄һклэӈӈк (āhkleŋŋk), Northern Sami áhkạlakkis (“Greenland shark”)), further borrowed Old Norse hákarl (compare Icelandic hákarl, Faroese hákallur, dialectal Norwegian håkall).
